items.stem: What is the value of |3 − 8|?
Explain why the equation |2x + 5| = −1 has no solutions.
items.answer: The modulus of any real number is zero or positive, so |2x + 5| ≥ 0 and can never equal −1.
items.markingKey: B1 |2x + 5| ≥ 0 for all x; B1 so cannot equal a negative number [2]

items.stem: Explain why squaring both sides is a valid method for solving |f(x)| = |g(x)| but may introduce extra solutions when solving |f(x)| = g(x).
items.answer: Both sides of |f| = |g| are non-negative, so squaring is reversible. With |f(x)| = g(x), squaring also gives solutions of |f(x)| = −g(x), which must be rejected if g(x) < 0.
items.markingKey: B1 both sides non-negative so squaring is reversible; B1 for |f| = g, solutions with g(x) < 0 must be rejected [2]

items.stem: Solve the inequality |3x + 1| < 11.
items.markingKey: M1 critical values from 3x + 1 = ±11; A1 −4, 10/3; A1 −4 < x < 10/3 [3]

items.stem: Solve the equation |5x + 6| = |4x − 9|.
items.markingKey: M1 squares both sides or forms 5x + 6 = ±(4x − 9); A1 x = −15; A1 x = 1/3 [3]

items.stem: The functions f and g are defined for all real x by f(x) = |3x + 4| and g(x) = |4x − 7|. (a) Solve the equation f(x) = g(x). (b) Hence solve the inequality f(x) < g(x).
items.markingKey: (a) M1 squares or uses ±; A1 x = 3/7; A1 x = 11 [3] (b) B1 FT x < 3/7 or x > 11 using the graphs or the quadratic [1]

items.stem: Which of these is the graph of y = |x| ?
options: an inverted V with vertex at the origin
a straight line through the origin with gradient 1
a V shape with vertex at the origin
a U-shaped parabola through the origin
items.answer: a V shape with vertex at the origin
items.markingKey: For x ≥ 0, y = x; for x < 0, y = −x, giving a V with vertex (0, 0).

items.stem: Felix solves the inequality |4x + 7| < 9 and writes the answer x < 1/2. Explain what is wrong with this answer and give the correct solution.
items.answer: Felix has only used 4x + 7 < 9 and ignored 4x + 7 > −9. Correct solution: −4 < x < 1/2.

items.stem: Describe how the graph of y = |f(x)| is obtained from the graph of y = f(x).
items.answer: Parts of the graph on or above the x-axis are unchanged; parts below the x-axis are reflected in the x-axis.
items.markingKey: B1 parts above unchanged; B1 parts below reflected in the x-axis [2]

items.stem: Explain why |x − a| < b, where b > 0, can be written as a − b < x < a + b.
items.answer: |x − a| is the distance of x from a on the number line, so x is less than b away from a, i.e. between a − b and a + b.
items.markingKey: B1 distance interpretation (or −b < x − a < b); B1 a − b < x < a + b [2]

items.stem: Noah solves the equation |x − 8| = 3x − 2 by squaring both sides and obtains x = −3 and x = 5/2. Explain why one of these values must be rejected, and state the solution.
items.answer: At x = −3 the right-hand side 3x − 2 = −11, which is negative, but a modulus cannot be negative. Solution: x = 5/2.
items.markingKey: M1 substitutes into 3x − 2 (or checks both sides); A1 x = −3 rejected since 3x − 2 < 0; B1 x = 5/2 only [3]

items.stem: Solve the equation |4x − 1| = 1.
items.markingKey: M1 4x − 1 = ±1; A1 both values [2]

items.stem: Solve the inequality |4x − 6| ≥ 11.
items.markingKey: M1 critical values from 4x − 6 = ±11; A1 −5/4, 17/4; A1 x ≤ −5/4 or x ≥ 17/4 [3]

items.stem: Solve the inequality |3x + 1| < 12.
Solve the equation |4x − 4| = |2x − 5|.
items.markingKey: M1 squares both sides or forms 4x − 4 = ±(2x − 5); A1 x = −1/2; A1 x = 3/2 [3]

items.stem: The functions f and g are defined for all real x by f(x) = |4x + 5| and g(x) = |3x − 3|. (a) Sketch, on the same diagram, the graphs of y = f(x) and y = g(x), stating the coordinates of the points where each graph meets the axes. (b) Hence solve the inequality f(x) > g(x). (c) State the number of solutions of the equation f(x) = 3, giving a reason.
items.answer: (a) V-shaped graphs: y = f(x) meets the axes at (−5/4, 0) and (0, 5); y = g(x) at (1, 0) and (0, 3). (b) x < −8 or x > −2/7 (c) 2
items.markingKey: (a) B1 V shape for f with vertex (−5/4, 0) and (0, 5); B1 V shape for g with vertex (1, 0) and (0, 3) [2] (b) B1 FT x < −8 or x > −2/7 using the graphs or the quadratic [1] (c) B1 2, since the horizontal line y = 3 cuts the V-shaped graph twice (3 > 0) [1]

items.stem: The functions f and g are defined for all real x by f(x) = |4x + 7| and g(x) = |x + 1|. (a) Sketch, on the same diagram, the graphs of y = f(x) and y = g(x), stating the coordinates of the points where each graph meets the axes. (b) Solve the equation f(x) = g(x). (c) Hence solve the inequality f(x) > g(x).
items.answer: (a) V-shaped graphs: y = f(x) meets the axes at (−7/4, 0) and (0, 7); y = g(x) at (−1, 0) and (0, 1). (b) x = −2 or x = −8/5 (c) x < −2 or x > −8/5
items.markingKey: (a) B1 V shape for f with vertex (−7/4, 0) and (0, 7); B1 V shape for g with vertex (−1, 0) and (0, 1) [2] (b) M1 squares or uses ±; A1 x = −2; A1 x = −8/5 [3] (c) B1 FT x < −2 or x > −8/5 using the graphs or the quadratic [1]

items.stem: When a polynomial p(x) is divided by (x − a), the remainder is
items.markingKey: Remainder theorem: p(x) = (x − a)q(x) + R, so R = p(a).

items.stem: Explain why the remainder when p(x) is divided by (x − a) is p(a).
items.answer: p(x) = (x − a)q(x) + R for a quotient q(x) and constant R. Putting x = a makes the first term zero, so p(a) = R.
items.markingKey: B1 p(x) = (x − a)q(x) + R; B1 substitute x = a gives R = p(a) [2]

items.stem: Explain why, when a polynomial is divided by (x − 1)(x + 2), the remainder can be written in the form px + q.
items.answer: The remainder must have degree less than the degree of the divisor, which is 2, so it is at most linear: px + q.
items.markingKey: B1 degree of remainder < degree of divisor; B1 divisor degree 2 so remainder linear [2]

items.stem: When 2x³ + x² + kx − 5 is divided by (x + 4), the remainder is −81. Find the value of the constant k.
items.markingKey: M1 substitutes x = −4 and equates to −81; A1 k = −9 [2]

items.markingKey: M1 long division (or equating coefficients) to a quadratic quotient; A1 quotient 3x² + 4x + 10; A1 remainder 26 [3]

items.stem: The polynomial p(x) is defined by p(x) = x³ + ax² + bx + 9, where a and b are constants. When p(x) is divided by (x + 1) the remainder is 19, and when p(x) is divided by (x + 3) the remainder is 39. (a) Find the remainder when p(x) is divided by (x − 3). (b) Find the remainder when p(x) is divided by (2x − 1).
When a polynomial p(x) is divided by (2x + 1), the remainder is
items.markingKey: Put 2x + 1 = 0: x = −1/2, so the remainder is p(−1/2).

items.stem: A cubic polynomial is divided by a quadratic. What is the greatest possible degree of the remainder?
items.markingKey: The remainder has degree less than the divisor, so at most 1 (linear).

items.stem: Diego divides p(x) = x³ − 6x² + 1 by (x² + 1) and says the remainder is the constant 7. Explain why the remainder could be linear, and find the correct remainder.
items.answer: The divisor has degree 2, so the remainder has degree at most 1. p(x) = (x² + 1)(x − 6) − x + 7; remainder −x + 7.
items.markingKey: B1 remainder degree < 2 so of the form px + q; B1 remainder −x + 7 [2]

items.stem: Explain how the remainder theorem can be used to find the remainder when p(x) is divided by (3x − 2) without long division.
items.answer: Find the value of x making the divisor zero, x = 2/3, and evaluate p(2/3); this equals the remainder.
items.markingKey: B1 x = 2/3 from 3x − 2 = 0; B1 remainder = p(2/3) [2]

items.stem: Elena says that the remainder when p(x) = 3x³ − 6x² + 1 is divided by (x + 1) is p(1) = −2. Explain the error and find the correct remainder.
items.answer: The divisor is zero when x = −1, so the remainder is p(−1) = −8.
items.markingKey: B1 x + 1 = 0 gives x = −1; B1 remainder −8 [2]

items.stem: When x³ − 6x² + kx − 2 is divided by (x − 3), the remainder is −44. Find the value of the constant k.
items.markingKey: M1 substitutes x = 3 and equates to −44; A1 k = −5 [2]

items.stem: When x³ + 2x² + kx + 7 is divided by (x + 1), the remainder is 11. Find the value of the constant k.
items.markingKey: M1 substitutes x = −1 and equates to 11; A1 k = −3 [2]

items.stem: The polynomial p(x) is defined by p(x) = x³ + ax² + bx + 1, where a and b are constants. When p(x) is divided by (x + 1) the remainder is 3, and when p(x) is divided by (x − 3) the remainder is −5. (a) Find the remainder when p(x) is divided by (x − 1). (b) Find the remainder when p(x) is divided by (2x − 1).
If p(3) = 0 for a polynomial p(x), which must be a factor of p(x)?
items.markingKey: Factor theorem: p(a) = 0 ⇔ (x − a) is a factor.

items.stem: Explain why, if p(a) = 0, then (x − a) is a factor of p(x).
items.answer: By the remainder theorem p(x) = (x − a)q(x) + p(a). If p(a) = 0 the remainder is zero, so (x − a) divides p(x) exactly.
items.markingKey: B1 p(x) = (x − a)q(x) + p(a); B1 remainder zero so (x − a) is a factor [2]

items.stem: Explain why an integer root of x³ + bx² + cx + d = 0 (b, c, d integers) must be a factor of d.
items.answer: If x = k is a root then k³ + bk² + ck = −d, so k(k² + bk + c) = −d and k divides d.
items.markingKey: B1 rearranges to k(k² + bk + c) = −d; B1 so k divides d [2]

items.stem: Given that (x + 4) is a factor of p(x) = 3x³ + 3x² − 30x + 24, factorise p(x) completely.
items.markingKey: M1 divides by (x + 4) to obtain a quadratic; A1 correct quadratic factor; A1 3(x + 4)(x − 1)(x − 2) [3]

items.stem: Show that (x − 5) is a factor of p(x) = 3x³ − x² − 75x + 25. Hence factorise p(x) completely.
items.markingKey: B1 p(5) = 0; M1 divides to obtain a quadratic; A1 quadratic factor; A1 (3x − 1)(x + 5)(x − 5) [4]

items.stem: The polynomial p(x) = x⁴ + 3x³ − 13x² − 27x + 36 has factors (x − 1) and (x + 4). Factorise p(x) completely.
items.markingKey: M1 divides by (x − 1)(x + 4) = x² + 3x − 4; A1 quadratic quotient; M1 factorises the quotient; A1 (x + 4)(x + 3)(x − 1)(x − 3) [4]

items.stem: The polynomial p(x) = x³ + ax² + bx − 60, where a and b are constants. It is given that (x − 5) is a factor of p(x), and that when p(x) is divided by (x − 3) the remainder is −84. (a) Find the values of a and b. (b) Solve the equation p(x) = 0.

items.markingKey: p(−1/3) = 0, so (3x + 1) is a factor.

items.stem: Sipho finds that p(5) = 0 for p(x) = x³ − 19x − 30, and concludes that (x + 5) is a factor. Explain the error and state the correct factor.
items.answer: p(5) = 0 means x = 5 is a root, so the factor is (x − 5); (x + 5) would need p(−5) = 0, but p(−5) = −60.
items.markingKey: B1 root x = 5 gives factor (x − 5); B1 p(−5) ≠ 0 or correct factor stated [2]

items.stem: Diego finds that p(−3) = 0 for p(x) = x³ + 4x² + x − 6, and concludes that (x − 3) is a factor. Explain the error and state the correct factor.
items.answer: p(−3) = 0 means x = −3 is a root, so the factor is (x + 3); (x − 3) would need p(3) = 0, but p(3) = 60.
items.markingKey: B1 root x = −3 gives factor (x + 3); B1 p(3) ≠ 0 or correct factor stated [2]

items.stem: Explain why a cubic polynomial with real coefficients must have at least one real linear factor.
items.answer: A cubic tends to +∞ at one end and −∞ at the other, so its graph crosses the x-axis at least once; at that root a, (x − a) is a factor by the factor theorem.
items.markingKey: B1 opposite end behaviour so crosses x-axis; B1 factor theorem gives linear factor [2]

items.stem: Isla finds that p(2) = 0 for p(x) = x³ − x² − 22x + 40, and concludes that (x + 2) is a factor. Explain the error and state the correct factor.

items.markingKey: B1 root x = 2 gives factor (x − 2); B1 p(−2) ≠ 0 or correct factor stated [2]

items.stem: Show that (x + 4) is a factor of x³ + x² − 16x − 16, and hence find the other two linear factors.

items.stem: Explain how the sign of the leading coefficient of a cubic determines the shape of its graph for large |x|.
items.answer: For large |x| the term ax³ dominates. If a > 0 the curve goes from bottom-left to top-right; if a < 0 it goes from top-left to bottom-right.

items.stem: Explain why the graph of y = (x + 1)²(x − 4) touches the x-axis at x = −1 but crosses it at x = 4.
items.answer: (x + 1)² does not change sign either side of x = −1, so y keeps the same sign and the curve touches; (x − 4) changes sign at x = 4, so the curve crosses.
items.markingKey: B1 squared factor does not change sign; B1 single factor changes sign [2]

items.stem: Noah sketches y = −(x + 1)(x − 5)(x + 3) starting at the bottom left and finishing at the top right. Explain the error.

items.stem: Explain your reasoning in each part. (a) Explain why an integer root of x³ + bx² + cx + d = 0 (b, c, d integers) must be a factor of d. (b) Explain why, if p(a) = 0, then (x − a) is a factor of p(x).
items.answer: (a) If x = k is a root then k³ + bk² + ck = −d, so k(k² + bk + c) = −d and k divides d. (b) By the remainder theorem p(x) = (x − a)q(x) + p(a). If p(a) = 0 the remainder is zero, so (x − a) divides p(x) exactly.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 rearranges to k(k² + bk + c) = −d; B1 so k divides d [2] (b) B1 p(x) = (x − a)q(x) + p(a); B1 remainder zero so (x − a) is a factor [2]
